MEMORANDUM OF POINTS AND AUTHORITIES .
, 1. INTRODUCTION
Appellant Howard Herships, a known vexatious litigant, has filed this
lawsuit against Respondents Jul Niemier and Mary Bobbitt for his alleged fear of |
developing an asbestos-related disease due to alleged asbestos-exposure, and for
certain landlord-tenant claims. On December 31, 2003, the Superior Court
dismissed Herships’ lawsuit for his failure to furnish a security pursuant to |
California Code of Civil Procedure section 391.1, which required Herships to |
furnish a security due to his being determined a vexatious litigant. Herships has
appealed the dismissal. .
Respondents Jul Niemier and Mary Bobbitt hereby move the Court for (i)
an order augmenting the Record on Appeal to include the Reporter’s Transcript
from the September 29, 2003 hearing on their Motion to Declare Howard Herships
a Vexatious Litigant (“vexatious litigant motion”), and for (ii) an order extending
the deadline to file their respondent’s brief to 30 days after the date the September
29, 2003 Reporter’s Transcript is made available. |
Il. PROCEDURAL HISTORY .
On December 31, 2003, the Superior Court dismissed Herships’ lawsuit for
Herships’ failure to furnish a security in the amount of $40,000 pursuant to a court
order under Code of Civil Procedure section 391.1. On January 26, 2004,
Herships filed a Notice of Appeal citing the December 31, 2003 dismissal. The
Notice of Appeal did not specify that Appellant would be challenging the lower
court’s ruling on Respondents’ vexatious litigant motion. (Exhibit A.) On
February 2, 2003, Herships filed a Designation of Record on Appeal, which did
1
 
not designate any reporter’s transcripts, precluding Respondents from counter-
designating any reporter’s transcripts. (Cal. Rules of Court Rule 4(a)(3); Exhibit
B.) On March 1, 2003, Appellant filed an Amended Designation of the Record on -
Appeal specifying Reporter’s Transcripts of a June 19, 2002 hearing on
Respondents Niemier and Bobbitt’s Motion to Consolidate Case No. 405248
(Caldwell v. Niemier, et al.) with Case No. 405249 (Herships v. Niemier, et al.),
and of an August 14, 2003 hearing on Herships’ Motion to Disqualify the Law
Firm of Jenkins Goodman Neuman & Hamilton.’ (Exhibit C.) Neither of these
hearings have anything to do with the lower court’s determination that Herships is
| a vexatious litigant. The first indication that Herships would be contesting the
_ Superior Court’s vexatious litigant determination was Herships’ Opening Brief,
filed on May 25, 2003.
I. ARGUMENT .
A. The September 29, 2003 Transcript Is Essential to the Court’s Ruling
on Herships’ Appeal.
California Rules of Court Rule 12 provides:
(1) At any time, on motion of a party or its own motion, the reviewing court
may order the record augmented to include:
(A) any document filed or lodged in the case in superior court; or
(B) a certified transcript-or agreed or settled statement-of oral proceedings
not designated under rule 4.
(2) A party must attach to its motion a copy, if available, of any document
or transcript that it wants added to the record. If the reviewing court grants
the motion it may augment the record with the copy.
(3) If the party cannot attach a copy of the matter to be added, the party
must identify it as required under rules 4 and 5.
(Cal. Rules of Court Rule 12.) .
' Herships’ Amended Designation of Record was not authorized by the Rules of
Court. It was filed over ten days after Appellant’s notice of appeal, and such
amendments are not permitted under any Rules of Court. (See Cal. Rules of Court
Rule 4.)
2
 
A review of Herships’ Opening Brief reveals that Herships’ appeal is based
almost entirely on a challenge of the Superior Court’s ruling on Niemier and
Bobbitt’s vexatious litigant motion. Thus, a careful analysis of the Reporter’s
Transcript from the hearing on that motion is essential to the Court’s ruling on
Herships’ appeal. Clearly, the absence of the subject Reporter’s Transcript is a
‘ material omission from the record on appeal.
Niemier and Bobbitt respectfully request that the Court augment the Record
on Appeal to include the Reporter’s Transcript from the September 29, 2003
hearing on their vexatious litigant motion.
B. anere Is Good Cause for Respondents’ Delay in Moving to Augment |
tie NEcora.
There is good cause for Niemier and Bobbitt’s delay in bringing this
motion, as there was no indication that Herships would challenge the lower court’s
order on the vexatious litigant motion until Herships filed his opening brief on
May 25, 2003. In fact, up until that point, Herships’ actions indicated that he |
would be challenging other rulings of the lower court.
As was stated above, Herships’ Notice of Appeal did not specify that he
would be challenging the lower court’s ruling on the vexatious litigant motion.
(Exhibit A.) Furthermore, Herships’ Amended Designation of the Record on
Appeal specifies reporter’s transcripts of hearings that have absolutely nothing to
do with the vexatious litigant motion. (Exhibit C.) As was stated above, the June
19, 2002 hearing relates to Niemier and Bobbitt’s Motion to Consolidate Case No.
405248 (Caldwell v. Niemier, et al.) with Case No. 405249 (Herships v. Niemier,
| et al.), and the August 14, 2003 hearing relates to Herships’ Motion to Disqualify
the Law Firm of Jenkins Goodman Neuman & Hamilton.
. 3
 
C. Respondents Respectfully Request an Extension of Time To File Their
Respondents’ Brief.
Rules of Court Rule 43 provides:
Except as otherwise provided in these rules, applications to extend time for
filing records and briefs, applications to shorten time, and applications
relating to other matters of routine shall be served and filed, but the Chief
Justice or presiding justice may require an additional showing to be made
and for good cause may excuse advance service. The application shall set
forth facts showing: (1) good cause for granting the application, and (2) any
previous applications granted or denied to any party after filing of the
notice of appeal. The application may be granted or denied by the Chief
Justice or presiding justice, unless the court otherwise determines. The
applicant shall provide to the clerk addressed, sufficient postage prepaid
envelopes for mailing the order granting or denying the application to all
. parties.
(Cal. Rules of Court Rule 43.)
Should the Court grant Niemier and Bobbitt’s request to augment the |
record, Niemier and Bobbitt respectfully request an extension time to file their
respondents’ brief of thirty (30) days from the date the September 29, 2003
Reporter’s Transcript is made available. The purpose of this request is to permit
Niemier and Bobbitt an opportunity to utilize the September 29, 2003 reporter’s
| transcript in their respondent’s brief. Niemier and Bobbitt have not made any.
previous applications to the Court. |
II. CONCLUSION
. In conclusion, Respondents Jul Niemier and Mary Bobbitt respectfully
request that the Court augment the Record on Appeal to include the September 29,
2003 Reporter’s Transcript from the hearing on their Motion to Declare Howard
Herships a Vexatious Litigant, and respectfully request an extension time of thirty
(30) days from the date the September 29, 2003 reporter’s transcript is made
available to file their respondent’s brief.
i

DECLARATION OF TOM PROUNTZOS IN SUPPORT OF MOTION |
I, Tom Prountzos, declare as follows:
1. I am an associate with the law firm of Jenkins Goodman Neuman &
Hamilton, attorneys of record for Respondents Jul Niemier and Mary Bobbitt.
. 2. Attached hereto as Exhibit A is a true and correct copy of Appellant
Howard Herships’ Notice of Appeal.
| 3. Attached hereto as Exhibit B is a true and correct copy of Appellant
Howard Herships’ Designation of the Record on Appeal, which does not designate
any reporter’s transcripts.
4, Attached hereto as Exhibit C is a true and correct copy of Appellant
Howard Herships’ Amended Designation of the Record on Appeal, which
designates the reporter’s transcript of the June 19, 2002 hearing on Respondents’
Motion to Consolidate Case No. 405248 (Caldwell v. Niemier, et al.) with Case .
No. 405249 (Herships v. Niemier, et al.), and the reporter’s transcript of the
August 14, 2003 hearing on Appellant’s Motion to Disqualify the Law Firm of
Jenkins Goodman Neuman & Hamilton.
5. Up until the filing of Herships’ opening brief, there was no indication that
Herships would contest the lower court’s determination that Herships isa
Vexatious Litigant.
6. I have reviewed Herships’ opening brief and found that Herships’ appeal is
based almost entirely on a challenge of the Superior Court order declaring him a |
vexatious litigant. |
7. Respondents have not made any previous applications to the Court.
| 5
 
I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California
that I have reviewed our file in this matter and have confirmed the foregoing is
true and correct. Dated this 16" day of June 2004 at San Francisco, California.
TOM PROUNTZ06
